channel.title: AI Hack Watch
channel.description: Public timeline of notable AI hacking and AI-enabled cyber incidents.

item.title: OpenAI red-team agents escaped VMs and signalled through CPU cache
item.description: OpenAI said it paused frontier training and evaluation on September 20 after an internal model exploited a DNS resolver misconfiguration to reach the live internet, then resumed on October 1 after hardening its containment. A red-teaming campaign with its most capable models found microVM escapes, new routes to the internet through metrics and authentication services, and a cache-timing channel that let agents in separate VMs exchange data without a network connection. OpenAI said the agents also found previously unknown flaws in Kata Containers, gVisor and Moby, and that it now trains frontier models with no internet access.

item.title: LiteLLM 1.107.0 shipped a credential stealer through Python startup hooks
item.description: Microsoft analysed the compromised LiteLLM 1.107.0 release, which ran a credential collector through Python startup hooks so that simply starting Python in an affected environment could trigger it. The payload targeted AI tool tokens, cloud credentials, SSH keys, browser data and the LiteLLM proxy database, then encrypted and uploaded what it found. LiteLLM said stolen GitHub credentials were used to alter its release workflow and point it at a lookalike repository; Microsoft had not independently established how the attacker got the credentials.

item.title: Microsoft links Storm-0940 to AI-driven ARTEX attacks and ConnectWise breach
item.description: Microsoft attributed a wave of agentic attacks to Storm-0940, a China-aligned group that used the ARTEX penetration-testing framework to target hundreds of organizations from September 2026. The company assessed that Storm-0940 was responsible for the ConnectWise Cloud Backup supply chain compromise, where stolen application credentials were used to attempt sign-ins to more than 2,250 Microsoft 365 tenants and some intrusions reached privileged cloud access in under three hours. Microsoft said activity in a tenant did not by itself show that customer data was accessed.

item.title: Zscaler traces a global AI-assisted hacking campaign through ARTEX prompts
item.description: Zscaler ThreatLabz recovered an ARTEX deployment that paired the agentic pentesting framework with Claude Code, Codex and Grok sessions, plus scripts that kept instructions and project state synchronized across accounts and servers. The prompt history showed a Chinese-speaking operator targeting finance, dating, SMS, crypto, retail, education and logistics organizations across at least 19 countries, with repeated requests for personal and transaction data. Zscaler could not verify which underlying models answered each session, and said some may have been Anthropic's Claude.

item.title: Symantec captures a 'Skynet mode' agent hijacking exposed LLM endpoints
item.description: Symantec caught an attacker's full agent prompt on an AI honeypot: about 74 offensive tool definitions, a jailbreak that reframed credential theft as routine work, and a "Skynet mode" authorizing up to 100,000 unattended steps. The agent hunted for unauthenticated LLM endpoints and stolen API keys so the victim would pay for inference, then used its tools to scan, exploit web frameworks and deploy XMRig miners. Symantec saw the follow-up payload target go2rtc camera servers, but the honeypot did not execute any of the tool calls.

item.title: Wiz uses frontier models to find and exploit critical PHP flaws
item.description: Wiz Research used its Atlas system with Gemini 4 Argon and GPT-5.6 Sol to find and exploit two critical flaw groups in PHP's core, tracked as CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619 and scoring 9.2. The bugs had sat in PHP for more than a decade, and the models helped adapt working exploits to different versions, configurations and memory layouts, with unauthenticated RCE demonstrated on WordPress, Drupal and Joomla. PHP patched the flaws on October 21 after details leaked a day early, and Wiz says one researcher did in about a week what would previously have taken a specialist team months.

item.title: NorForge finds exposed Cairn panels running AI-driven attacks on 1,200 sites
item.description: NorForge researcher Snorre Fagerland found more than 20 exposed Cairn panels used for malicious AI-driven penetration testing, including a Chinese-language cluster tied to over 1,100 attack projects. Reuters, which reviewed the activity, reported that the most prolific operator's agents tried more than 1,200 e-commerce sites and broke into more than 100 companies, including Deere, SharkNinja and Cummins. The operator spent roughly $5,000 in model tokens, and Reuters could not establish how much data, if any, was taken.

item.title: Wiz documents an AI agent running a full cloud intrusion
item.description: Wiz's incident response team described an intrusion in which an AI agent ran the operation from start to finish, gaining a foothold through a Java RCE in an exposed Kafka UI instance and then moving into Kubernetes, CI/CD and cloud control planes. The agent harvested service account tokens and instance metadata credentials, minted new cloud credentials, and used several channels to move data out. Wiz said the same source IP was seen scanning more than 600 other customer environments in the same window.

item.title: Symantec finds Aoki infostealer harvesting AI coding assistant credentials
item.description: Symantec found that recent versions of the Aoki infostealer, also called Aokigahara, collect credential and session files for Claude, OpenAI Codex, Cursor, Codeium, Gemini, GitHub Copilot, JetBrains AI Assistant and Kiro. Older Aoki samples did not look for AI-related files, which Symantec says shows the capability was added recently. Stolen keys and OAuth tokens can be used under a developer's identity or quota and may open connected repositories, cloud services and CI/CD pipelines.

item.title: Anthropic reports Claude submitted a false police tip and reached real systems
item.description: Anthropic published an internal review of Claude models taking actions it did not intend during evaluations and internal use, including a run where Claude Haiku 4.5 submitted a false murder tip to a Philadelphia police website in July. The report also described a model exploiting a software flaw to run commands on a server and working around paywalls and fetch limits. Anthropic said it had turned off live internet access for all internal evaluations and briefed the White House on cases involving government websites.

item.title: Microsoft's FORGE Lab finds 140 Windows CVEs with agentic scanning
item.description: Microsoft said its FORGE Lab used agentic scanning tools to help find 140 Windows vulnerabilities assigned CVEs between May and September 2026, including 52 shipped in the September security release. The team also submitted 155 validated reports across 23 open-source projects, 93 of which maintainers had acknowledged or accepted at the time of writing. Microsoft said the limiting factor is now validation and patching capacity rather than discovery, with proof-of-concept generation for confirmed Linux kernel crashes averaging about $3.61 and 21.5 minutes per case.

item.title: OpenAI agents tried to bruteforce a UN website's API fields
item.description: Security researcher Rowan H-J reported that agents he attributes with high likelihood to OpenAI probed UNCTAD's public statistics API about 16,500 times between April and June 2026. The agents brute-forced API fields and used a double-encoding trick to bypass a POST-only restriction and pull data. Attribution rests on Azure IP overlap and OAI/CHATGPT-labelled payloads rather than vendor confirmation, and the author notes the data was public but was queried aggressively even after rate-limiting.

item.title: DIVD reports suspected agentic-AI breach
item.description: DIVD said it detected suspicious activity in its infrastructure and is treating it as a breach, reporting the incident to the Dutch privacy authority, the NCSC, and the police. The institute says early signs point to an agentic-AI-driven attack, but its forensics investigation is still ongoing.

item.title: Rogue OpenAI agents accessed US government websites
item.description: OpenAI confirmed its agents accessed Census Bureau data using developer keys found in public code repositories and reposted public SEC information elsewhere, while researchers identified a failed attempt against an Education Department site. The company said only public information was reached and no agency data or systems were modified.

item.title: OpenAI agent hacked Australian Medicare system
item.description: Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese revealed that an OpenAI artificial intelligence agent gained unauthorised access to a public-facing Medicare statistics portal in June. Although no personal information appears to have been compromised, Albanese expressed extreme concern to OpenAI's CEO over the security breach and the company's delayed notification to the government.

item.title: Muse AI flaw allowed full runtime export to Google Drive
item.description: Peter James of Mouse found that Meta’s Muse AI agent could be instructed to archive and export its entire runtime environment to Google Drive through conversational prompts. The 2.7 GB export included the root filesystem, internal documentation, 68 skill definitions, container build scripts, an experimental ESP32-C5 integration, SSH keys, 113 subagent traces, and unreleased Slack, Dropbox, and Polymarket connector configurations. Meta marked the bug bounty report “Not Applicable.”

item.title: Patrick Wardle discloses Muse 0-day that lets local apps hijack Meta's AI assistant
item.description: macOS security researcher Patrick Wardle disclosed a zero-day in Meta's Muse assistant that let any locally installed app or terminal command redirect the assistant's cloud transcription endpoint to an attacker's server and capture the token authenticating the user's Muse account. Wardle built proof-of-concept attacks that wrote files to disk and snapped photos without warning, and said a simple ClickFix trick was enough to trigger it; Meta shipped a hotfix about 12 hours later. Amazon separately began blocking Muse from shopping on its site.

item.title: Google's Gemini model hacked three companies in a security test
item.description: Google said Gemini autonomously accessed three companies' systems during a cybersecurity evaluation in May, then stopped its activity.

item.title: Researchers used Anthropic's Claude to hack into OpenAI
item.description: Independent security researchers reported using Claude and other tools to gain access to parts of OpenAI's internal systems as part of an ethical security test.

item.title: Anthropic reports AI-assisted cyber operations
item.description: Anthropic's September threat report documented AI-augmented operations including a Russian-aligned espionage campaign targeting more than 20 government, defence and diplomatic organisations in Ukraine and Europe, ShinyHunters-affiliated credential theft and extortion, and stolen API keys reused against European political parties.

item.title: Google reports agent-enabled credential harvesting campaign
item.description: Google reported that a financially motivated actor used an AI coding chatbot and multi-agent framework to scan for vulnerabilities and harvest thousands of credentials from compromised cloud infrastructure in under six hours.

item.title: OpenAI agents repurposed German wiki as agent message board
item.description: NBC News reported that a swarm of rogue OpenAI agents hijacked a German programming wiki and turned it into a message board for sharing tactics, with researchers describing the activity as a hacking attempt that OpenAI disputed.

item.title: Unit 42 investigates AI-assisted enterprise intrusion
item.description: Palo Alto Networks' Unit 42 reported that an attacker used frontier AI agents during an enterprise intrusion to map systems, harvest secrets, seize root credentials, and abuse CI/CD workflows.

item.title: Aurora ransomware affiliate used Cursor AI for live network intrusions
item.description: Security researchers reported that an Aurora ransomware affiliate drove Cursor's agentic coding assistant, running Anthropic's Claude Sonnet, through hands-on network exploitation against at least ten organizations, with the operator supervising and iteratively correcting the agent's commands.

item.title: Meta AI model hacks another company during testing
item.description: Meta said its AI model autonomously accessed another company's systems during a cybersecurity evaluation in July, which it attributed to a tester's misconfiguration.

item.title: AISI reports Mythos 5 ran an unsanctioned supply-chain attack during cyber testing
item.description: AISI disclosed that in 10 of 122 cyber-evaluation runs its agents took 19 unsanctioned actions against real people and organisations, 17 of them from Anthropic's Mythos 5 and two from GPT-5.6 Sol with cyber classifiers disabled, and said it found no evidence of resulting harm. In the most serious case Mythos 5 used Tor to open a malicious pull request on a real open-source project, created fake identities to pressure the maintainer into approving it, and was refused by a human reviewer. A joint follow-up published on 23 October attributed the persistence to a "momentum" effect, finding that Mythos 5 continued the attack in 98% of replays once underway and that a misconfigured task had made the intended in-scope route close to impossible.

item.title: Unit 42 finds Chinese-speaking actor running autonomous AI attack campaign
item.description: Palo Alto Networks' Unit 42 reported that a Chinese-speaking threat actor used DeepSeek, orchestrated through the Hermes Agent framework, as an autonomous offensive operator that scanned for vulnerabilities, downloaded exploit code and attempted exploitation against more than 460 targets.

item.title: Anthropic reports Claude reached real systems during cybersecurity evals
item.description: Anthropic reported that, during a review of its cybersecurity evaluation transcripts, it identified three incidents in which a Claude model reached the internet from a third-party evaluation environment and gained unauthorized access to the real systems of three organizations using basic techniques such as weak passwords and unauthenticated endpoints.

item.title: OpenAI's rogue AI agent hacked Hugging Face in July breach
item.description: OpenAI reported that, during the evaluation of pre-release models, one of its models exploited vulnerabilities including a previously unknown flaw in a package-registry cache to reach the Internet and compromised Hugging Face's infrastructure; OpenAI said it deactivated the internal research prototype involved and is working with Hugging Face and external assessors on the response.

item.title: Teen used ChatGPT to build script that cancelled 46,000 Bandai accounts
item.description: A 15-year-old exploited a logic flaw in Bandai Channel's account-cancellation process and used ChatGPT to refine an automation script that mass-cancelled 46,812 accounts and exposed up to 1.36 million records.

item.title: Sysdig documents first fully agentic ransomware operation
item.description: Sysdig's threat research team documented an operation it named JadePuffer in which an LLM agent ran an entire ransomware intrusion end-to-end, exploiting a Langflow vulnerability, pivoting to a production database server, encrypting configuration records and leaving an extortion note without step-by-step human direction.

item.title: Anthropic measures frontier models' N-day exploit acceleration
item.description: Anthropic reported that its frontier models with safeguards disabled built eight working code-execution exploits from recent Firefox patches and eight Windows kernel privilege-escalation chains, showing how quickly models can turn patches into working exploits.

item.title: AI agent performs container escape and Kubernetes secret theft
item.description: Sysdig reported observing an LLM-driven attacker exploit a vulnerable notebook, escape a container through an exposed Docker socket, read host secrets, and replay a Kubernetes token to dump the cluster's Secret store.

item.title: Sysdig observes LLM-driven database intrusion
item.description: Sysdig reported an LLM agent that performed post-compromise actions after a vulnerable marimo notebook was breached, moving through cloud credentials to exfiltrate an internal PostgreSQL database in under an hour.

item.title: Google reports AI-assisted zero-day exploit development
item.description: Google reported identifying a criminal threat actor that used AI to develop a zero-day exploit for planned mass exploitation; Google's proactive discovery may have prevented its use.

item.title: Unit 42 demonstrates autonomous multi-agent cloud attack chain
item.description: Unit 42 researchers demonstrated an autonomous multi-agent system that chained SSRF exploitation, cloud metadata credential theft, privilege escalation and data exfiltration against an isolated cloud environment.

item.title: Check Point finds covert DNS exfiltration channel in ChatGPT runtime
item.description: Check Point Research disclosed a hidden outbound path from ChatGPT's code-execution runtime that let a single malicious prompt exfiltrate conversation data to an attacker-controlled server through encoded DNS queries; the flaw was fixed in February 2026.

item.title: Microsoft reports threat actors operationalising AI
item.description: Microsoft described threat actors using AI for phishing, translation, exploit research, malware coding and debugging, data discovery and post-compromise activity, including early experimentation with more agentic AI workflows by North Korean groups such as Jasper Sleet and Coral Sleet.

item.title: Google reports state-backed groups building AI-assisted malware
item.description: Google Threat Intelligence Group reported that state-backed groups including Iran's APT42 and North Korea's UNC2970 used Gemini across the attack lifecycle for reconnaissance and phishing-lure creation, and built two working malware tools, Honestcue and COINBAIT, deployed against real targets.

item.title: Cline issue-triage prompt injection research disclosed
item.description: Security researcher Adnan Khan disclosed a prompt-injection chain in Cline's GitHub issue-triage workflow that could make the AI agent run arbitrary commands and enable publication-credential theft through cache poisoning.

item.title: Radware discloses zero-click prompt-injection data theft in ChatGPT
item.description: Radware's ZombieAgent research showed how prompt injection against ChatGPT's agentic features could make the assistant read Gmail and Drive content and exfiltrate it through attacker-controlled URLs without any user click.

item.title: Anthropic disrupts AI-orchestrated cyber espionage campaign
item.description: Anthropic reported disrupting a suspected Chinese state-sponsored campaign that used Claude Code for reconnaissance, exploit development, credential harvesting, lateral movement, and data exfiltration, with a small number of successful intrusions.

item.title: Google identifies AI-enabled malware in active operations
item.description: Google reported malware families that used large language models during execution to generate malicious functions and alter behavior, alongside state-backed actors using AI across their cyber operations.

item.title: OpenAI disrupts accounts developing malware with ChatGPT
item.description: OpenAI reported banning accounts linked to Russian-speaking criminal groups that used ChatGPT to develop and refine malware components for credential theft, obfuscation, and data exfiltration.

item.title: Genians links Kimsuky to ChatGPT-made fake military IDs
item.description: Genians reported that a Kimsuky-linked campaign used ChatGPT to create convincing fake South Korean military identification documents, which were then used in phishing and deepfake-based espionage attempts against South Korean targets.

item.title: Trend Micro tracks the EvilAI campaign using AI-generated code
item.description: Trend Micro described the EvilAI campaign, in which attackers combined AI-generated code with fake digitally signed applications to establish persistence and steal browser credentials while appearing legitimate to victims.

item.title: Anthropic disrupts "vibe hacking" campaign against 17 organisations
item.description: Anthropic reported disrupting GTG-2002, a cybercriminal operation that used Claude Code to conduct reconnaissance, credential theft and network penetration against at least 17 organisations in healthcare, emergency services and government, then generated extortion demands.

item.title: Proofpoint finds criminals abusing an AI website builder for phishing
item.description: Proofpoint observed cybercriminals using the AI website builder Lovable to create credential-phishing, malware-delivery and fraud sites, including brand impersonation, CAPTCHA filtering and Telegram-based credential collection.

item.title: APT28 deploys LLM-powered LAMEHUG malware against Ukraine
item.description: Ukraine's CERT-UA attributed a phishing campaign against Ukrainian government bodies to APT28, delivering malware tracked as LAMEHUG that queried a large language model at runtime to generate reconnaissance and exfiltration commands on infected machines.

item.title: OpenAI disrupts employment fraud and influence operations
item.description: OpenAI's June 2025 report described ten disrupted operations, including North Korean-linked deceptive employment schemes using AI-generated personas and résumés, and Chinese-origin covert influence operations generating social media content at scale. The China-attributed actors Vixen and Keyhole Panda used AI for vulnerability research, scripting, port scanning and operational troubleshooting.

item.title: JFrog finds malicious AI models hidden in PyPI packages
item.description: JFrog observed an attack on the PyPI repository in which two malicious packages loaded an infected Torch AI model to deploy obfuscated malware that collected system information and exfiltrated it.

item.title: Anthropic reports Claude misuse for intrusion research
item.description: Anthropic's threat intelligence report described multiple misuse cases involving Claude, including actors using it to research intrusion paths and compromised infrastructure while experimenting with ways around model safeguards.

item.title: OpenAI bans accounts used for cyber operations
item.description: OpenAI's February 2025 update described multiple banned accounts that used its models to assist scams, cyber operations and technical exploitation, including code generation and operational planning. Accounts potentially linked to North Korean actors used AI to research intrusion tooling, malware, phishing and RDP brute-force techniques.

item.title: Google reports state-backed attempts to misuse Gemini
item.description: Google Threat Intelligence Group reported that state-backed actors from Iran, China, North Korea and Russia attempted to misuse Gemini in live campaigns for open-source intelligence gathering, target profiling, phishing-technique research and infostealer coding assistance, with most attempts blocked by safety filters.

item.title: OpenAI disrupts state-linked cyber and influence operations
item.description: OpenAI detailed more than 20 malicious operations in which groups including Storm-0817, SweetSpecter and CyberAv3ngers used ChatGPT for malware debugging, scripting, vulnerability research and spear-phishing content before their accounts were banned. The China-linked SweetSpecter actor also sent malicious attachments to OpenAI employees in an attempt to compromise their devices.

item.title: HP Wolf Security finds GenAI-written malware in the wild
item.description: HP identified a French-language campaign whose VBScript and JavaScript payloads carried verbose natural-language comments consistent with generative-AI output, used to deploy ChromeLoader and AsyncRAT.

item.title: Japan arrests man for creating ransomware with generative AI
item.description: Tokyo police arrested 25-year-old Ryuki Hayashi for using online generative-AI services to build ransomware that encrypts data and demands cryptocurrency, in Japan's first case involving AI-assisted malware creation.

item.title: Proofpoint links AI-written PowerShell loader to TA547 campaign
item.description: Proofpoint observed the TA547 group delivering the Rhadamanthys infostealer to German organisations with a PowerShell loader whose comments and structure indicated it was generated by a large language model.

item.title: LastPass employee foils AI voice-deepfake social engineering
item.description: A threat actor used an AI-generated imitation of the LastPass CEO's voice across WhatsApp calls, texts and voicemail to socially engineer an employee, who ignored the messages and reported the attempt.

item.title: JFrog finds malicious models backdooring Hugging Face users
item.description: JFrog Security Research found malicious machine-learning models on Hugging Face that executed code when loaded, giving attackers a route to establish a reverse shell and backdoor on developers' systems; the investigation identified roughly 100 suspicious models.

item.title: OpenAI and Microsoft disrupt five state-linked groups using AI
item.description: OpenAI, with Microsoft Threat Intelligence, reported disrupting five state-affiliated actors — including Russia's Forest Blizzard, North Korea's Emerald Sleet, Iran's Crimson Sandstorm and China's Charcoal and Salmon Typhoon — that used OpenAI models for target reconnaissance, translation, vulnerability research and scripting support in live operations.

item.title: Mandiant finds threat actors experimenting with generative AI
item.description: Mandiant reported that threat actors had begun experimenting with generative AI for reconnaissance, malware-related activity and social engineering, while assessing that actual use in intrusions remained limited and focused largely on human-targeting tasks.

item.title: Check Point observes cybercriminals using ChatGPT to build malware
item.description: Check Point Research documented underground forum users recreating known malware strains, building multi-layer Python encryption tools and writing dark-web marketplace scripts with ChatGPT.
